newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse November turnover 7 pct down m/m.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse November turnover 7 pct down m/m.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange reported on Monday a 7.28 percent decline in its November turnover and traders cited tight liquidity as the key problem behind the fall.
Total turnover fell to 52.2 million dinars ($10.2 million) from 56.3 million in October, while the number of transactions remained unchanged at 179, the bourse said.

"Liquidity of the market deteriorated after the central bank increased the reserve requirement to 15 percent and majority of deals are based on revolving earlier borrowing," Natasa Bulajic of the Podgorica-based bourse told Reuters.
Short-term securities accounted for 27.3 million dinars or 52.23 percent of the monthly total, with companies' short-term bonds generating 27 million dinars.
Interest rates on those securities ranged between an annual 301.32 and 464.36 percent.
The giro-money market segment, where banks trade their surplus liquidity, accounted for 24.9 million dinars or 47.77 percent of the November total, the bourse said.
The bourse reported no trade in the central bank short-term bonds for the second consecutive month. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
